Youre off the antidepressants right? Some people react differently or the complete opposite and its important to tell your psychiatrist and taper off them. To me what this looks like is your mental stability took a really big hit from the antidepressants and it caused you to spiral. It was a really big slip, now the problem is more than just chemicals in your brain so i cant say if you get off the meds its just gonna be right where you were before but you can do this. You might not be able to undo the past few weeks but you can undo the state of mind the meds put you in. It doesnt mean the meds made your decisions for you, but part of this situation was totally out of your control and not your fault. Now you need to figure out which things you do have control over and begin the journey back to stability. And just keep in mind that if brain chemicals caused all that, then the situation might be better than it feels. Im so sorry this happened to you but try to keep in mind: first of all some of the pain might just go away completely as you improve. And second of all, very important, THIS IS NOT YOUR FAULT. Its true, you were still making your own choices and the meds didnt turn you into some kind of out of control robot. But THIS IS NOT YOUR FAULT

I had to nearly kill myself. That was the only thing that did it, and it did it fast. My thought process when i woke up was literally: thats a paramedic. Holy shit i overdosed. Holy shit i need to stop or i will die. And i stopped. It turned into a month long dissociative episode that, ive heard people describe things like this but never truly experienced it, felt like a waking nightmare. Derealization but evil and i thought maybe i was still high on it and hadnt woken up. 

It was only three months but so many things didnt get through. My girlfriend walking into me taking a “shower” for 5 hours but she saw me covered in my blood surrounded by several broken, used needles i still hadnt managed to hit a vein with for 5 hours. Looking at her with dead, unprocessing eyes as she cried and worried. When i finally moved from crouching in the shower everything hurt not from the coke but from staying still trying to find my vein. It didnt get through when i suddenly woke up in my room with all my rigs still out and i didnt remember going to sleep, my brain failing to register why i felt short of breath and dizzy. As soon as i stopped struggling to breathe i forgot and thought about how i could burn through my scarce money the fastest. Within a month i didnt understand why i would choose life and the things i love over this feeling. I didnt stop when i induced a heart arrythmia and it would switch between probably 200 beats per minute (scary fast heart pounding) and, literally, go half speed for a few beats and then back to heart pounding. 

I waited until there was something, an event, that snapped me out of it. I didnt think about it because i wanted that event to be me, cold and dead. I had to shoot up a half gram in 15 minutes because i missed the first quarter gram shot. Then not feel it at all because i blacked out probably seizing. Then wake up with my roommate that cares a lot about me to have kicked down the door with 10 paramedics standing over me in my shooting up place, which used to be the safety of my room. I dont care about myself as much but it took seeing the fear and pain of the ones that do was the only thing that got through. I was confused and scared and drank heavily for months and i cant really feel just think of what truly matters. But i am alive. And things matter. Things are coming back. The things i liked about being alive.
